name: TX-12
label: Likely R

key_factors: Strong Republican district with an R+11 partisan lean
Incumbent Craig Goldman running with a large cash advantage ($1.5M on hand)
Prediction markets price Republican win at ~95%
No polling or expert ratings to suggest competitive race
model.rationale: Goldman combines incumbency, a heavily Republican seat, and a dominant fundraising edge, while markets price his win near 95% and no polls or ratings point to competition. The forecast stays close to the fundamentals-based margin of roughly R+15.
model.watch: Any credible polling showing the Democrat within single digits, or a major scandal or outside spending surge against Goldman, would warrant revisiting.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
TX-12 is a solidly Republican Fort Worth–area seat, and first-term incumbent Craig Goldman is running for reelection after winning his party's nomination. He enters the general election with about $1.5 million on hand and modest outside support, while Democrat Angela Rodriguez Prilliman has reported little fundraising activity. No public general-election polls or expert race ratings are available for this contest.

Prediction markets give Goldman roughly a 95% chance of winning, consistent with the district's Republican lean and his incumbency and financial advantages. The expected margin is around fifteen points Republican, with meaningful uncertainty given the absence of polling, but the race is rated Safe Republican.
